title: Integrating climate, market and behavioural processes strengthens bio-economic modelling for ecosystem-based fisheries management
content:
Abstract
Bio-economic models are widely used to assess the impacts of fisheries management strategies and explore biological, ecological, and economic trade-offs. However, many applications rely on simplified assumptions that limit their ability to inform management under changing climatic and socio-economic conditions. This study presents a tuned and transferable bio-economic framework developed within the European project SEAwise to evaluate fisheries management strategies under the interacting effect of climate change, market dynamics, and policy drivers. The framework integrates climate-driven changes in stock productivity with enhanced representations of fish price dynamics, métier-specific cost structures, and a common set of economic, social, and environmental indicators. It is applied to large-scale and small-scale mixed fisheries across multiple European case studies, including the North Sea, Celtic Seas, Bay of Biscay, and the Mediterranean Sea. The framework also evaluates a range of management strategies, including the fishing mortality corresponding to the maximum sustainable yield (FMSY)- and Pretty Good Yield (PGY), technical measures, and spatial management. Across regions and socio-economic scenarios, results show that management strategies based on FMSY generally provide more robust outcomes under climate and market uncertainty, compared to other strategies, particularly in terms of carbon intensity and distributional effects across small-scale and large-scale fisheries. PGY strategies, instead, can deliver conditional short- to medium-term economic gains under favourable socio-economic scenarios representing alternative future development pathways. The framework also includes behavioural sub-models, illustrated through selected case studies. By jointly assessing economic performance, carbon intensity, and food provision, the framework supports the operationalization of ecosystem-based fisheries management and provides a transparent, replicable approach for evaluating management strategies under climate and socio-economic uncertainty.
